sections.h2: Which part of Southampton is your house in?
sections.html:
Southampton is a large town at the eastern end of Suffolk County, wrapped by the Atlantic Ocean on its south side and Peconic Bay on the north. It covers 293.46 square miles, but only 139.13 of those are land. English settlers from Lynn, Massachusetts founded it in 1640, and the area is widely known as the Hamptons. The town keeps an online map of more than 100 historic markers and districts, which is worth a look if your house is an old one.

The town is a collection of smaller places, and the one on your deed matters more than the town name. Seven incorporated villages sit inside it: North Haven, Quogue, Sag Harbor (partly), Sagaponack, Southampton, Westhampton Beach and West Hampton Dunes. The unincorporated hamlets include Bridgehampton, East Quogue, Flanders, Hampton Bays, North Sea, Noyack, Remsenburg, Riverside, Shinnecock Hills, Speonk, Tuckahoe and Water Mill. A house in an incorporated village may answer to the village's own code office as well as the town.

Southampton is expensive, and many of its houses are lived in by owners who plan to stay. The typical owner-occupied value is $928,100, with 82.4% of homes owner-occupied and 90.8% of residents in the same house a year earlier. Gross rent is typically $2,363 a month.

  • Population on July 1, 2025: 71,601, up 3.7% from the 2020 base.
  • Households: 26,576, averaging 2.55 people.
  • Typical household income: $128,594.

A value near $928,100 sits just under the $1 million line that triggers New York's extra mansion tax, so the exact sale price can change what the buyer owes at the closing table. Price your house with that threshold in mind.

sections.h2: Coastal weather and an older house
sections.html:
With about 49.8 inches of precipitation and 26.8 inches of snow a year, about 114 days of measurable precipitation and a shoreline on two sides, moisture is a fact of life for houses here. Keep receipts for roof, siding, drainage and mechanical work, and gather repair paperwork after any storm damage so a buyer's inspector can see what was done and when.

A cash buyer will often take a weathered house as it stands, without asking you to finish the work first, which matters if you do not want to manage contractors through a coastal winter.

sections.h2: Selling a house that has been rented
sections.html:
You can, but the town's rental permit rules shape how you sell it. Any dwelling rented for any period needs a rental permit, and the Town Code sets a minimum stay of 14 days. Shorter stays count as transient rentals, which the code does not allow. There is no maximum stay.

Southampton rental permit rules
QuestionTown answer
Is a permit needed?Yes, for any home rented for any period
Minimum stay14 days
How long is a permit good?Two years
Does it transfer to a new owner?No, a new owner needs a new permit
Processing timeAbout 1 to 3 weeks, 2 to 4 in summer
Where are applications dropped off?27 Ponquogue Ave., Hampton Bays

Because permits do not pass to a buyer, an investor purchasing a rental has to apply in their own name, and moving a property into an LLC, trust or estate also requires a new permit. Advertising a house for rent without a permit can bring violations, suspension or revocation, and a two-year ban on renting.

There are two routes to a permit. A Standard application is inspected by a New York State certified code enforcement officer from the town's Department of Public Safety. A Certified application uses an architect or engineer the owner hires, and expedited processing is also offered. An owner of a single-family house may rent up to two bedrooms to no more than two renters without a permit, as long as the owner lives there and everyone shares the kitchen and living space.

sections.h2: Property tax dates, penalties and exemptions
sections.html:
Bills leave the Town Receiver of Taxes by December 15. The first half is due January 10 and the second May 31. You can pay at the counter, online, or by mail if the postmark is on or before the due date. An online e-check costs $1.75, and cards carry a 2.5% processor fee.

Paying late hurts. Money sent after January 10 still reaches the Receiver, but 1% interest builds every month. Once May 31 passes, a 5% penalty and 5% interest are added and the town stops taking payment, so the balance moves to the Suffolk County Treasurer's Office in Riverhead, 631-852-3000.

  • Exemption applications, including STAR and the senior and disability exemptions, are due March 1.
  • Grievance Day is the third Tuesday in May, and the Assessor's Office at 116 Hampton Road can help at 631-283-6020.
  • Property details and amounts due are searchable on the town's eTax portal by address, owner's last name, tax map number or bill number, and a duplicate bill can be requested there.
  • Unpaid taxes do not sit forever: the county typically starts collection on vacant land after one year and on improved property after three.

Each side is credited or charged at closing for its share of the tax year, so get current balances before you sign the contract.

Sellers here owe the state transfer tax, and buyers owe a local charge. The state rate is $2 for each $500 of price, paid by the seller. A buyer owes the 1% mansion tax only on residential prices of $1 million or more.

The town also runs the Community Preservation Fund, which is financed by a two percent real estate transfer tax paid by the purchaser, not the seller. At recording, the county clerk requires a Peconic Bay Region Community Preservation form with every recording in the five East End towns, which are Riverhead, Southampton, East Hampton, Shelter Island and Southold. Both parties sign it.

The Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead files the deed along with the RP-5217 transfer report and the TP-584 return. Your attorney supplies the deed form, since the clerk sells none, and each party must show a street address, never a P.O. box.

First decide who your likely buyer is and what stays with the house. A rented property needs its permit status confirmed, and the buyer should hear early that the permit does not follow the sale. Print your current tax bill from the eTax portal to see what is paid, and set aside repair receipts.

Next your attorney drafts the deed, listing a street address for each party, and sends it with the TP-584, RP-5217 and Community Preservation forms to the clerk in Riverhead. At the closing table the tax year is divided by date between you and the buyer, and state transfer tax is deducted from your proceeds. Cash deals have no lender appraisal or approval to wait on, so you can usually pick the day.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental permit to sell a house I rented out?
faqs.a: A permit is not required to sell, but it is required to rent. Permits last two years and cannot be passed to a buyer, so the new owner applies for their own.

faqs.q: How much interest is added if taxes are late?
faqs.a: After January 10, first-half taxes accrue 1% interest per month. After May 31 a 5% penalty and 5% interest apply, and the balance is collected by the Suffolk County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Who pays the Community Preservation Fund fee?
faqs.a: The buyer pays it. The clerk still requires the Peconic Bay Region form, signed by both parties, with the recording.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Southampton house for a weekend?
faqs.a: Not under the town code. The minimum rental stay is 14 days, and anything shorter counts as a transient rental that is not allowed.

faqs.q: When is the deadline for tax exemptions?
faqs.a: March 1 for exemption filings, including STAR and the senior and disability exemptions. Applications go to the Assessor's Office.
